key_insight: Non-binary detector error models preserve circuit-fault correlations and represent any Pauli channel exactly, while enabling more compact graphs and improved decoding.
engineering_relevance: Tanner graphs with 4–5× fewer edges can reduce hardware interconnect demands, while scalar belief-propagation messages keep communication per edge simple.
method: Represent each fault location with one random variable over its original error alphabet.
Apply a split-merge-regroup transformation to compact Clifford-circuit detector error models.
Decode using belief propagation, optionally with ordered-statistics decoding (OSD) post-processing.
evidence_signal: Numerical evaluations on surface, color, and bivariate bicycle codes report improved decoding performance, 4–5× fewer graph edges, and up to 9.4× faster CPU execution for BP with OSD.
watch_item: The reported speedup is a best-case CPU result; hardware gains and performance across other noise models require validation.
